verdict.summary: Creating a public connection and authorizing your own account is quick and needs no review. The effort is in the gates after that: Notion's Marketplace listing needs a security review, an 'Any workspace' installation scope that cannot be changed later, and a listing draft. The docs also say the authorization URL only appears after submission for review, which may block your own test.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-3 hours to reach Gate 1 and 2; plus about half a day for listing assets and forms if you pursue Gate 3
verdict.time_to_first_connection: About 15-30 minutes if the authorization URL is available; otherwise blocked until the connection is submitted for review (see blockers)
verdict.approval_wait: None reported for unlisted use. Marketplace listing: Notion expects to respond within 5-10 business days; security review timeline not found.

gates.name: Your own workspace (development connection)
gates.unlocks: You create the public connection, copy its client credentials, and connect your own Notion account through Composio.
limits: You must be able to create connections in the development workspace; the docs say a workspace owner is required to create a connection.
The Authorization URL field populates only after the public connection is submitted for review, so the OAuth test may be blocked at this gate.
Installation scope cannot be changed after creation, so choose it deliberately.

gates.name: Unlisted public connection (invited or other users)
gates.unlocks: Other Notion users and workspaces can authorize your connection through its OAuth flow without a Marketplace listing.
limits: Each user who authorizes gets their own access token and must complete the flow individually.
No official user cap or install cap for unlisted public connections was found in the docs fetched.
Community sources report an average of 3 requests per second per integration, returning HTTP 429 when exceeded.
Token expiry is unclear: current docs describe refresh tokens, while an older guide says access tokens never expire. Verify with a real exchange.
gates.time_to_reach: Same day as Gate 1 once the authorization URL is available

gates.name: Marketplace listing (public to anyone)
gates.unlocks: Your connection can be listed in Notion's Marketplace and discovered by any workspace.
limits: Only public connections with installation scope 'Any workspace' are eligible; selected-workspace connections cannot be listed.
Public connections must pass a Notion security review before listing; its questionnaire and timeline were not found.
Rejections can cite brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or unmet baseline criteria. You can revise and resubmit.
Listing is optional; the connection works through OAuth without it.
gates.time_to_reach: Several days to weeks, including the 5-10 business day listing response and any security review

steps.title: Decide managed Composio app or your own public connection
steps.detail: Use Composio's managed Notion OAuth app if you only need to connect your own account. Register your own public connection if you need your own client credentials, branding, or a Marketplace listing later.
gotchas: Listing is optional, so you do not need a listing to run your own OAuth flow.

steps.title: Confirm the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: Open your Composio dashboard and copy the redirect URI for the Notion auth config. Composio's toolkit record and its Notion guide list different defaults, so use the one shown in your dashboard.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Notion requires the redirect URI in the connection to match the one used in the token request.

steps.title: Open the Notion Developer portal
steps.detail: Go to app.notion.com/developers/connections and sign in with the Notion account that owns the development workspace. The older my-integrations URL now redirects to this page.
gotchas: The page is JavaScript-only, so use a current browser with scripts enabled.
The docs say a workspace owner is required to create a connection.

steps.title: Create the public connection
steps.detail: In the sidebar, open Build, then select Public connections. Enter the connection name, choose the development workspace, add the redirect URI, and pick the installation scope and capabilities.

values.label: Installation scope
values.value: Any workspace (required if you plan to list on the Marketplace; cannot be changed later)

values.label: Capabilities
values.value: Choose only the read, update and insert capabilities your app needs

gotchas: Notion does not use OAuth scope strings. Access comes from capabilities and the pages each user selects in the picker.
Scope cannot be changed after creation, so decide before you save.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI on the connection
steps.detail: Add the Composio callback URL as the redirect URI on the public connection. Do not use URL fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or a public IP address.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Copy the client credentials
steps.detail: Open the connection's Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and client secret. Store the secret in your secrets manager, not in source control.
gotchas: The Authorization URL field may stay empty until the connection is submitted for review. If it is empty, see the blockers section.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in Composio and connect your account
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Notion auth config that uses your client ID and secret. Start a connection with your own Notion account and choose the pages to share in the picker.
gotchas: Notion's token exchange uses HTTP Basic auth built from the client ID and secret.
If the flow cannot start because no authorization URL exists, you cannot complete Gate 1 until the connection is submitted for review.

steps.title: Check token behavior with a real exchange
steps.detail: Run one authorization and token exchange, then record whether a refresh token is returned and whether the access token expires. Confirm the refresh behavior before relying on it in production.
gotchas: An older third-party guide says there are no refresh tokens and no expiry. Treat that as outdated until your own exchange shows otherwise.

steps.title: Test with a second user and a second workspace
steps.detail: Have another Notion user, ideally in a different workspace, complete the flow. Confirm they get their own token and see only the pages they select.
gotchas: Each member who authorizes must complete the flow individually.

steps.title: Watch the rate limit
steps.detail: Send a short burst of requests through one token and check for HTTP 429 responses. Build retry with backoff into your client before inviting users.
gotchas: The 3 requests per second figure comes from community sources. The official rate-limit page was not fetched, so confirm it.

steps.title: Draft listing assets and legal links
steps.detail: Draft the listing name, description, category, tags, and short copy. Also draft or collect the privacy policy, terms of use, and support email, plus logo and images.
gotchas: Older third-party guides name the privacy policy, terms and support email as required fields. Confirm the current list in the listing form.

steps.title: Fill in the Marketplace listing and submit
steps.detail: Open Listings > Connections, create a draft listing attached to your public connection, fill in the details and assets, and submit it for review.
gotchas: Only connections with 'Any workspace' scope can be listed.

steps.title: Wait for the listing response
steps.detail: Notion says it expects to reply by email within 5-10 business days. Track status on the Listings > Connections page.

steps.title: Revise and resubmit if rejected
steps.detail: If rejected, read the email, fix the cited issue (brand or trademark, quality, or baseline criteria), and resubmit from the same page.
gotchas: Brand or trademark problems are a common cause of rejection.

requirements.item: Redirect URI with a protocol, no fragments, relative paths, wildcards or public IP
requirements.detail: Use the Composio callback URL from your dashboard. It must match the redirect URI in the token request.

requirements.item: Workspace owner access to create a connection
requirements.detail: Docs say you must be a workspace owner to create a connection. Confirm that your account meets this in the development workspace.

requirements.item: Authorization URL visible in Configuration tab
requirements.detail: The docs say the Authorization URL populates only after the public connection is submitted for review.

requirements.item: Installation scope set to Any workspace
requirements.detail: Required for Marketplace listing. Cannot be changed after creation, and selected-workspace connections are not eligible.
Public connections must pass a security review before Marketplace listing. The questionnaire and timeline were not found.

requirements.item: Listing details, category, tags, images and logo
requirements.detail: Required for the listing draft and submitted from Listings > Connections.

requirements.item: Privacy policy, terms of use and support email
requirements.detail: Named by older third-party guides as required. Confirm in the current listing form.

scopes.scope: Connection capabilities (read content, update content, insert content, etc.)
scopes.effect: Set in the Developer portal when you create the connection. They define what the integration can do. Choose the minimum your app needs; the docs do not describe a review tier for capabilities.

scopes.scope: Installation scope: Any workspace vs selected workspaces
scopes.effect: Cannot be changed after creation. Only Any workspace connections can be listed on the Marketplace.

scopes.scope: Per-user page selection in the picker
scopes.effect: Each user chooses which pages to share during authorization. Access is limited to those pages.
Notion does not use scope strings. A third-party guide says no OAuth scope is required by default.

blockers.symptom: Authorization URL field is empty in the Configuration tab, so you cannot start the OAuth flow from your own connection.
blockers.cause: Notion's docs say the Authorization URL populates only after the public connection is submitted for review.
blockers.fix: Confirm whether submitting for review is required before your own test. If it is, submit the connection for review, or use Composio's managed Notion app for Gate 1 testing.

blockers.symptom: Requests return HTTP 429 when sent in bursts.
blockers.cause: Community sources report an average limit of 3 requests per second per integration, with bursts allowed.
blockers.fix: Add retry with backoff and throttle requests. Confirm the official limit and whether it applies per token or per workspace.

blockers.cause: Rejections can cite brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or unmet baseline criteria.
blockers.fix: Read the rejection email, fix the cited issue, and resubmit from Listings > Connections.

blockers.symptom: Connection cannot be listed on the Marketplace even though it works.
blockers.cause: Only public connections with 'Any workspace' scope can be listed, and the scope cannot be changed after creation.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with Any workspace scope if you need a listing. The existing connection can still be used through OAuth without a listing.

blockers.symptom: An invalid client ID does not produce an OAuth error in the browser.
blockers.cause: The authorize endpoint redirected to the install-integration page with HTTP 200 and no error parameter when probed with an invalid client ID.
blockers.fix: Do not rely on the browser step to validate credentials. Confirm the client ID and secret with a real token exchange.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed OAuth app if you only need to connect your own account or ship to your own users. Register your own public connection when you need your own OAuth client or branding, or when you plan to list on the Marketplace. Notion has no OAuth scope strings; access is set by connection capabilities and per-user page selection in the picker. Confirm the Composio redirect URI in your Composio dashboard before configuring, because Composio's toolkit record and its Notion guide list different defaults.

evidence.quote: Listing on the Marketplace is optional

evidence.claim: The authorization flow starts by sending the user to the connection's authorization URL with owner=user, client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code.
The token exchange POSTs to the Notion token endpoint with HTTP Basic auth built from the client ID and secret. The body carries grant_type, code and redirect_uri when required.
Redirect URIs must have a protocol and cannot contain fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or a public IP address.
evidence.quote: It can't contain URL fragments, relative paths or wildcards, and can't be a public IP address.

evidence.claim: Notion's token response includes an access token, a refresh token, a bot_id, the owner user object and workspace fields. Refreshing returns a new access token and a new refresh token.
evidence.quote: Notion responds with an access_token, refresh_token, and additional information.

evidence.claim: An older third-party guide says Notion returns no refresh token and access tokens never expire. This conflicts with current docs and should be treated as outdated unless a real exchange confirms it.
evidence.quote: The Notion OAuth API doesn't support refreshing tokens, and so doesn't return a refresh token.

evidence.claim: Notion does not use OAuth scope strings. Access is granted through connection capabilities set in the Developer portal, and users pick specific pages in the picker.
evidence.quote: Connection capabilities (read content, update content, insert content, etc.)

evidence.claim: A third-party guide says no OAuth scope is required by default for Notion integrations.
evidence.quote: No OAuth scope is required by default for Notion integrations.

evidence.claim: Each user who authorizes a public connection gets their own access token, and each workspace member must complete the flow individually.
evidence.quote: each user who authorizes the connection receives their own access token, scoped to their workspace.

evidence.claim: A personal access token can be made in the Developer portal for personal scripts. It acts as its creator and has no OAuth flow, so it cannot serve other users.
evidence.quote: Use a PAT when a script, CLI workflow, Worker, or trusted tool should act as you.

evidence.claim: Probing the authorize endpoint with an invalid client ID redirected to the install-integration page with HTTP 200 and no OAuth error parameter.
Public connections need Notion's security review before Marketplace listing. No separate verification or minimum-install requirement was found for an unlisted public connection.
evidence.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Listing requires a public connection with Any workspace scope and a logo and images. Older third-party guides name a privacy policy, terms of use and support email as required.
evidence.quote: add the links to a privacy policy, terms of use, and finally, a support email.

evidence.claim: Notion's public API is rate-limited to an average of 3 requests per second per integration with bursts allowed; exceeding it returns HTTP 429. The official page was not fetched.
evidence.quote: The rate limit for incoming requests per integration is an average of three requests per second.

evidence.claim: Community reports say Notion may apply different rate limits by pricing plan. No official plan-based install cap for unreviewed public connections was found.
evidence.quote: Notion may introduce distinct rate limits for workspaces in different pricing plans.

open_questions: Does Notion require submitting the public connection for review before any OAuth flow works, including your own test? The docs say the Authorization URL appears only after submission, which conflicts with the note that unlisted use is allowed.
Notion's official rate-limit page was not fetched. The 3 requests per second figure is from community sources. Confirm the limit and whether it applies per token or per workspace.
No official user cap or install cap was found for unlisted or unreviewed public connections.
The security review's questionnaire, scope and timeline were not found. They are separate from the 5-10 business day listing response.
